cat > /analysis-results/analysis-summary.md << 'SUMMARY'
# jvm-tools (SJK) Analysis of Apache Tika

## Overview
This report presents the results of running **Swiss Java Knife (SJK)** - the `jvm-tools` suite by aragozin - against a running Apache Tika JVM process.

## Tool Information
- **Tool**: jvm-tools (Swiss Java Knife / SJK)
- **Repository**: https://github.com/aragozin/jvm-tools
- **Version**: 0.24-SNAPSHOT (built from source)
- **Build**: Maven with JDK 8 toolchain

## Target Project Information
- **Project**: Apache Tika
- **Repository**: https://github.com/apache/tika
- **Version**: 4.0.0-SNAPSHOT
- **Java**: OpenJDK 21.0.11 (Ubuntu)
- **Build**: Maven 3.9.9

## Analysis Setup
A test Java program (`TikaAnalysis.java`) was created that exercises Tika's core functionality:
- File type detection (text/plain, PDF, HTML)
- Content parsing and text extraction
- The program ran in a loop with JMX remote management enabled (port 9010)
- SJK attached to the running JVM process via local attach API and JMX

## SJK Commands Executed

### 1. jps - JVM Process Listing
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar jps --csv --process-details PID,MAIN,FQDN_MAIN,ARGS`
**Output**: `jps-output.csv`
- Listed all local JVM processes including the TikaAnalysis process

### 2. ttop - Thread Top (CPU/Memory monitoring)
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar ttop -p <pid> -n 30 -ri 5s`
**Output**: `ttop-output.txt`
- Monitored thread CPU usage, memory allocation rates
- Key findings:
  - Process CPU: ~15-37%
  - Main thread allocated ~11MB/s
  - 14 threads total
  - RMI/JMX threads consumed minimal CPU

### 3. hh - Heap Histogram
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar hh -p <pid> -n 30`
**Output**: `heap-histogram-output.txt`
- Top heap objects by instance count:
  - `org.apache.tika.mime.MediaType`: 6,928 instances
  - `org.jsoup.parser.Tag`: 6,710 instances
  - `org.apache.tika.mime.MimeType`: 1,685 instances
  - `org.apache.tika.detect.MagicDetector`: 1,381 instances
  - `org.apache.tika.io.TikaInputStream`: 605 instances

### 4. hh --live - Live Objects Heap Histogram
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar hh -p <pid> -n 50 --live`
**Output**: `heap-histogram-live-output.txt`
- Showed surviving (live) objects after GC:
  - `org.apache.tika.mime.MimeType`: 1,685 instances (94KB)
  - `org.apache.tika.detect.MagicDetector`: 1,381 instances (66KB)
  - `org.apache.tika.mime.MediaType`: 1,912 instances (61KB)
  - Total live: 11,503 instances, 426KB

### 5. vminfo - VM Information Dump
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar vminfo -p <pid> --agentprops --flags --perf --sysprops`
**Output**: `vminfo-output.txt`
- Dumped all JVM flags (G1 GC, 288 processors detected)
- Agent properties, performance counters, system properties

### 6. mx - MBean Queries (JMX)
**Commands**: Various `java -jar sjk.jar mx -p <pid> -b <bean> -mg -f <attr>`
**Outputs**: `mx-memory-output.txt`, `mx-threading-output.txt`, `mx-gc-output.txt`, `mx-classloading-output.txt`, `mx-os-output.txt`, `mx-runtime-output.txt`
- Memory: Heap used ~93MB, committed ~272MB, max ~30GB
- Threading: 16 threads (15 daemon), peak 16
- GC: G1 Young Generation - 7 collections, 135ms total
- Class loading: 6,280 loaded classes, 0 unloaded
- OS: Linux 6.8.0-87-generic, amd64, 288 processors
- Runtime: OpenJDK 21, Ubuntu, management spec 4.0

### 7. gc - GC Tracker
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar gc -p <pid>`
**Output**: `gc-output.txt`
- Real-time GC monitoring showing memory pool changes per collection
- G1 Young Generation collection events tracked

### 8. mxdump - Full JMX MBean Dump
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar mxdump -p <pid> -q "java.lang:*"`
**Output**: `mxdump-output.txt`
- Complete JSON dump of all java.lang:* MBeans (799 lines)
- Includes memory pools, GC stats, threading, runtime, OS, class loading

### 9. mxping - JMX Connection Verification
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar mxping -p <pid>`
**Output**: `mxping-output.txt`
- Verified JMX connectivity to target JVM

### 10. stcap - Stack Trace Capture
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar stcap -p <pid> -o tika-stack-dump.bin -i 100ms -t 15s -l 50`
**Output**: `tika-stack-dump.bin`
- Captured 60 stack trace samples at 100ms intervals
- Binary format dump for further analysis

### 11. ssa --histo - Stack Sample Histogram
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar ssa -f tika-stack-dump.bin --histo --sort OCCUR`
**Output**: `ssa-histogram-output.txt`, `ssa-histogram-csv.csv`
- Frame frequency analysis showing most common call paths
- Main thread spending time in Thread.sleep and Tika parsing

### 12. ssa --thread-info - Per-Thread Summary
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar ssa -f tika-stack-dump.bin --thread-info`
**Output**: `ssa-thread-info-output.txt`
- Per-thread CPU, allocation, and state breakdown
- Main thread: 4.5% CPU, 12MB/s allocation
- RMI connection: 8% CPU, 2.7MB/s allocation

### 13. ssa --print - Raw Stack Trace Printing
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar ssa -f tika-stack-dump.bin --print`
**Output**: `ssa-print-output.txt`
- Full text dump of all captured stack traces (649 lines)

### 14. flame - Interactive HTML Flame Graph
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar flame -f tika-stack-dump.bin -o tika-flame-graph.html`
**Output**: `tika-flame-graph.html` (142KB)
- Interactive HTML flame graph visualization

### 15. ssa --flame - SVG Flame Graph
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar ssa -f tika-stack-dump.bin --flame --title "Tika Analysis Flame Graph"`
**Output**: `tika-flame-graph.svg` (29KB)
- SVG flame graph for static viewing

### 16. dexp - Dump Export
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar dexp -f tika-stack-dump.bin --export-all -csv`
**Output**: `dexp-output.csv`
- Tabular CSV export of all metrics from the stack dump

## Key Findings

### Memory Usage
- Tika creates significant transient objects during parsing (~11MB/s allocation rate on main thread)
- MediaType and MimeType objects dominate the heap, reflecting Tika's MIME type registry
- jsoup Tag objects are also numerous (HTML parsing)
- Live object retention is modest after GC (~426KB), indicating efficient garbage collection

### CPU Usage
- Main thread (Tika parsing loop) consumed ~5-6% CPU
- RMI/JMX threads consumed minimal CPU for monitoring overhead
- G1 GC runs frequently (young generation) but with very low pause times (~12-19ms per collection)

### Thread Profile
- 16 threads total (15 daemon)
- Main thread: parsing + Thread.sleep (control loop)
- Standard JVM threads: Reference Handler, Finalizer, Common-Cleaner, Signal Dispatcher
- JMX infrastructure: RMI TCP Accept, RMI TCP Connection, JMX server connection timeout threads
- HttpClient selector for network operations

### Class Loading
- 6,280 classes loaded, 0 unloaded
- Tika's extensive parser framework loads many classes at startup

Swiss Java Knife (SJK)
=========

SJK is a command line tool for JVM diagnostic, troubleshooting and profiling.

SJK exploits standard diagnostic interfaces of JVM (such as JMX, JVM attach and perf counters) and adds some more logic on top 
useful for common troubleshooting cases. SJK can also be used as a library for building application specific diagnostic tools
or to enhance your code with self monitoring features.

What you can do with SJK?
----

 - [Monitor Java threads in real time][ttop]
 - [Analyze head dynamics with advanced class histograms][hh]
 - [Access MBean attributes and operation from command line][mx]
 - Create [flame graphs][html-flame] and over reports from snapshots created VisualVM, Java Flight Recorder or [SJK's own sampler][stcap]
 
See [full command reference](sjk-core/COMMANDS.md).

Download
----

Latest prebuild binaries [![Last Version](https://img.shields.io/maven-central/v/org.gridkit.jvmtool/sjk.svg)](https://search.maven.org/#search%7Cga%7C1%7Cg%3A%22org.gridkit.jvmtool%22)
- `wget https://training.ragozin.info/sjk.jar` -> [sjk.jar](https://search.maven.org/remotecontent?filepath=org/gridkit/jvmtool/sjk-plus/0.22/sjk-plus-0.22.jar) 

Starting sjk
----

    java -jar sjk.jar <cmd> <arguments>
    java -jar sjk.jar --commands
    java -jar sjk.jar --help <cmd>

Below a few command from SJK ([full command reference](sjk-core/COMMANDS.md)).

[ttop]
----

Pools thread CPU usage of the target JVM and periodically reports to the console.

 - can attach via PID or open JMX port
 - displays thread memory allocation rate and cumulative process allocation rate
 - displays safe point time consumption (only if attache via PID)

[More details][ttop]

[hh]
----

Similar to `jmap -histo`.

 - plus can show a histogram of dead objects (histograms of all and live requested, then difference is calculated)
 - plus can show N top buckets in histogram

[More details][hh]

[stcap], [stcpy], [ssa] and [flame]
----

These commands provide basic sample profiler capabilities. `stcap` produces hyper-dense stack trace dump 
(about 1000 compression rate compared to text format) and `ssa` provides few reports over dump files.
`stcpy` can copy data in archives produced by `stcap` (e.g. merging dumps or filtering selected threads).

So far following reports are available:

 - [sophisticated filtering] (time, stack trace, thread name)
 - stack frame histogram with advanced filtering options
 - flame graph visualization (SVG or [interactive HTML][html-flame])
 - per thread summary (CPU usage, memory allocation, etc)
 - converting back to text format

Dump file can be also processed programatically.

[More details][ssa]

messages.reasoning_content:
Tika requires Java 17+. The current default Java is Java 21, which should work. Let me build tika-core (the main module) first, then use jvm-tools to analyze it.

jvm-tools (SJK) is primarily a JVM diagnostic tool - it can analyze running JVMs, thread dumps, heap histograms, GC logs, JFR files, etc. To use it on the tika project, I need to:

1. Build tika (at least partially)
2. Run the tika application or a test with SJK monitoring it
3. Or use SJK to analyze the built artifacts

Let me think about the best approach:
- I could build tika-core and then use SJK's `hh` (heap histo) or `ttop` commands to monitor a running tika process
- I could use SJK to analyze JFR files if I can generate them
- I could use SJK's `ssa` command to analyze thread dumps

Let me first try to build tika-core at least, then run a simple tika command while using SJK to monitor it.

Actually, let me think more carefully. SJK is a JVM diagnostic tool. The most straightforward way to "run it on the project tika" would be:
1. Build tika
2. Run a tika process (e.g., tika-app)
3. Use SJK to monitor/analyze the running JVM (e.g., using ttop, hh, or gc commands)

Or alternatively, I could use SJK to analyze the jar files themselves. But SJK doesn't really analyze code - it analyzes running JVMs.

Let me try building tika-app first (it might be too large to build the whole thing), then run it and use SJK to monitor it.

{"command": "cat > /analysis-results/analysis-summary.md << 'SUMMARY'
# jvm-tools (SJK) Analysis of Apache Tika

## Overview
This report presents the results of running **Swiss Java Knife (SJK)** - the `jvm-tools` suite by aragozin - against a running Apache Tika JVM process.

## Tool Information
- **Tool**: jvm-tools (Swiss Java Knife / SJK)
- **Repository**: https://github.com/aragozin/jvm-tools
- **Version**: 0.24-SNAPSHOT (built from source)
- **Build**: Maven with JDK 8 toolchain

## Target Project Information
- **Project**: Apache Tika
- **Repository**: https://github.com/apache/tika
- **Version**: 4.0.0-SNAPSHOT
- **Java**: OpenJDK 21.0.11 (Ubuntu)
- **Build**: Maven 3.9.9

## Analysis Setup
A test Java program (`TikaAnalysis.java`) was created that exercises Tika's core functionality:
- File type detection (text/plain, PDF, HTML)
- Content parsing and text extraction
- The program ran in a loop with JMX remote management enabled (port 9010)
- SJK attached to the running JVM process via local attach API and JMX

## SJK Commands Executed

### 1. jps - JVM Process Listing
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar jps --csv --process-details PID,MAIN,FQDN_MAIN,ARGS`
**Output**: `jps-output.csv`
- Listed all local JVM processes including the TikaAnalysis process

### 2. ttop - Thread Top (CPU/Memory monitoring)
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar ttop -p <pid> -n 30 -ri 5s`
**Output**: `ttop-output.txt`
- Monitored thread CPU usage, memory allocation rates
- Key findings:
  - Process CPU: ~15-37%
  - Main thread allocated ~11MB/s
  - 14 threads total
  - RMI/JMX threads consumed minimal CPU

### 3. hh - Heap Histogram
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar hh -p <pid> -n 30`
**Output**: `heap-histogram-output.txt`
- Top heap objects by instance count:
  - `org.apache.tika.mime.MediaType`: 6,928 instances
  - `org.jsoup.parser.Tag`: 6,710 instances
  - `org.apache.tika.mime.MimeType`: 1,685 instances
  - `org.apache.tika.detect.MagicDetector`: 1,381 instances
  - `org.apache.tika.io.TikaInputStream`: 605 instances

### 4. hh --live - Live Objects Heap Histogram
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar hh -p <pid> -n 50 --live`

  - `org.apache.tika.mime.MimeType`: 1,685 instances
  - `org.apache.tika.detect.MagicDetector`: 1,381 instances
  - `org.apache.tika.io.TikaInputStream`: 605 instances

### 4. hh --live - Live Objects Heap Histogram
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar hh -p <pid> -n 50 --live`
**Output**: `heap-histogram-live-output.txt`
- Showed surviving (live) objects after GC:
  - `org.apache.tika.mime.MimeType`: 1,685 instances (94KB)
  - `org.apache.tika.detect.MagicDetector`: 1,381 instances (66KB)
  - `org.apache.tika.mime.MediaType`: 1,912 instances (61KB)
  - Total live: 11,503 instances, 426KB

### 5. vminfo - VM Information Dump
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar vminfo -p <pid> --agentprops --flags --perf --sysprops`
**Output**: `vminfo-output.txt`
- Dumped all JVM flags (G1 GC, 288 processors detected)
- Agent properties, performance counters, system properties

### 6. mx - MBean Queries (JMX)
**Commands**: Various `java -jar sjk.jar mx -p <pid> -b <bean> -mg -f <attr>`
**Outputs**: `mx-memory-output.txt`, `mx-threading-output.txt`, `mx-gc-output.txt`, `mx-classloading-output.txt`, `mx-os-output.txt`, `mx-runtime-output.txt`
- Memory: Heap used ~93MB, committed ~272MB, max ~30GB
- Threading: 16 threads (15 daemon), peak 16
- GC: G1 Young Generation - 7 collections, 135ms total
- Class loading: 6,280 loaded classes, 0 unloaded
- OS: Linux 6.8.0-87-generic, amd64, 288 processors
- Runtime: OpenJDK 21, Ubuntu, management spec 4.0

### 7. gc - GC Tracker
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar gc -p <pid>`
**Output**: `gc-output.txt`
- Real-time GC monitoring showing memory pool changes per collection
- G1 Young Generation collection events tracked

### 8. mxdump - Full JMX MBean Dump
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar mxdump -p <pid> -q "java.lang:*"`
**Output**: `mxdump-output.txt`
- Complete JSON dump of all java.lang:* MBeans (799 lines)
- Includes memory pools, GC stats, threading, runtime, OS, class loading

### 9. mxping - JMX Connection Verification
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar mxping -p <pid>`
**Output**: `mxping-output.txt`
- Verified JMX connectivity to target JVM

### 10. stcap - Stack Trace Capture
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar stcap -p <pid> -o tika-stack-dump.bin -i 100ms -t 15s -l 50`
**Output**: `tika-stack-dump.bin`
- Captured 60 stack trace samples at 100ms intervals
- Binary format dump for further analysis

### 11. ssa --histo - Stack Sample Histogram
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar ssa -f tika-stack-dump.bin --histo --sort OCCUR`
**Output**: `ssa-histogram-output.txt`, `ssa-histogram-csv.csv`
- Frame frequency analysis showing most common call paths
- Main thread spending time in Thread.sleep and Tika parsing

### 12. ssa --thread-info - Per-Thread Summary
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar ssa -f tika-stack-dump.bin --thread-info`
**Output**: `ssa-thread-info-output.txt`
- Per-thread CPU, allocation, and state breakdown
- Main thread: 4.5% CPU, 12MB/s allocation
- RMI connection: 8% CPU, 2.7MB/s allocation

### 13. ssa --print - Raw Stack Trace Printing
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar ssa -f tika-stack-dump.bin --print`
**Output**: `ssa-print-output.txt`
- Full text dump of all captured stack traces (649 lines)

### 14. flame - Interactive HTML Flame Graph
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar flame -f tika-stack-dump.bin -o tika-flame-graph.html`
**Output**: `tika-flame-graph.html` (142KB)
- Interactive HTML flame graph visualization

### 15. ssa --flame - SVG Flame Graph
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar ssa -f tika-stack-dump.bin --flame --title "Tika Analysis Flame Graph"`
**Output**: `tika-flame-graph.svg` (29KB)
- SVG flame graph for static viewing

### 16. dexp - Dump Export
**Command**: `java -jar sjk.jar dexp -f tika-stack-dump.bin --export-all -csv`
**Output**: `dexp-output.csv`
- Tabular CSV export of all metrics from the stack dump

## Key Findings

### Memory Usage
- Tika creates significant transient objects during parsing (~11MB/s allocation rate on main thread)
- MediaType and MimeType objects dominate the heap, reflecting Tika's MIME type registry
- jsoup Tag objects are also numerous (HTML parsing)
- Live object retention is modest after GC (~426KB), indicating efficient garbage collection

### CPU Usage
- Main thread (Tika parsing loop) consumed ~5-6% CPU
- RMI/JMX threads consumed minimal CPU for monitoring overhead
- G1 GC runs frequently (young generation) but with very low pause times (~12-19ms per collection)

### Thread Profile
- 16 threads total (15 daemon)
- Main thread: parsing + Thread.sleep (control loop)
- Standard JVM threads: Reference Handler, Finalizer, Common-Cleaner, Signal Dispatcher
- JMX infrastructure: RMI TCP Accept, RMI TCP Connection, JMX server connection timeout threads
- HttpClient selector for network operations

### Class Loading
- 6,280 classes loaded, 0 unloaded
- Tika's extensive parser framework loads many classes at startup
